The phrase 'based on' indicates a conditional (guard) on the transition. The exact closed-model carrier transition:line:24 has guard=null. The condition is instead encoded as an opaque trigger event, which is a different typed field. In UML statechart semantics, a state-based boolean condition that enables a transition is a guard, not a trigger. The trigger field represents events, while the guard field represents conditions on system state. The NL's 'dist_to_front<25 and extra_lane=true' is a state condition, properly a guard.

This is a state-based boolean condition (distance and velocity are system state variables), which in UML is properly expressed as a guard. The exact carrier transition:line:72 has guard=null. The condition is folded into a single opaque trigger event string that cannot be independently evaluated. A trigger represents an external event occurrence, while a guard represents a condition on system state. The NL's 'dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30' is a state condition, not an event, and thus requires guard encoding.

semantic_adjudication.basis: NL12 requirement quote listing multiple independent conditions, PlantUML source line 42 single label, closed model event declaration as single opaque token, UML trigger/guard semantics
semantic_adjudication.reason: The PlantUML source line 42 uses a single transition label: 'pedestrian_detected | (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30) | (dist_to_front<15 in hwy mode or <10 in urban mode)'. In PlantUML semantics, the text after the colon is one trigger field. The closed model correctly declares this as a single opaque event. The NL requires each condition to independently enable the transition (using 'or' to list alternatives). In UML, independently triggerable conditions require either separate transitions with distinct triggers/guards, or a single transition with a disjunctive guard. A single opaque event string cannot be decomposed at runtime, so none of the individual conditions can trigger the transition on its own. The strongest rebuttal ('the closed model is consistent with itself') addresses provenance but not the NL violation - the model fails to provide the NL-required independent condition enforcement.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL12 requires each activation condition (pedestrian_detected, dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30, dist_to_front<15 in hwy mode or <10 in urban mode) to be a separately triggerable or guardable condition, but the PlantUML source folds all conditions into a single opaque event label.

additional_contracts.quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
additional_contracts.reason: The NL describes CollisionAvoidanceSystem as an operational system with an initial state and activation behavior. The complete FCSTM reachability facts show it is unreachable from any top-level initial entry. No transition in the model connects AutonomousMode or any of its descendants to CollisionAvoidanceSystem, and no concurrent region separator establishes orthogonality. Without root reachability, the system's specified behavior can never execute, making this a causal global property absent from the NL-only contract plan (which only covers the local initial entry).

result.reason: Cross-view structural audit compared all 40 supplied contracts against the complete FCSTM closed model, source inventory, and deterministic facts. All containment, endpoint, and termination contracts are satisfied by exact model edges or state hierarchies. Two structural defects were identified in the CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope: (1) the NL-required initial entry to collision_avoidance_deactive is absent from the complete transition inventory (the compiler-generated synthetic UnspecifiedInitial is targeted instead), and (2) the entire CollisionAvoidanceSystem composite is unreachable from the model root because no transition or concurrent region connects it to the AutonomousMode subsystem. The strongest rebuttal ('the closed model is consistent with itself') addresses provenance but not the NL violation - the model fails to provide the NL-required independent condition enforcement.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL states the transition occurs 'when certain conditions are met, such as... the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30).' This is a state-based boolean condition (distance and velocity are system state variables), which in UML is properly expressed as a guard. The exact carrier transition:line:72 has guard=null. The condition is folded into a single opaque trigger event string that cannot be independently evaluated. A trigger represents an external event occurrence, while a guard represents a condition on system state. The NL's 'dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30' is a state condition, not an event, and thus requires guard encoding.

semantic_adjudication.basis: NL12 requirement quote listing multiple independent conditions, PlantUML source line 42 single label, closed model event declaration as single opaque token, UML trigger/guard semantics
semantic_adjudication.reason: The PlantUML source line 42 uses a single transition label: 'pedestrian_detected | (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30) | (dist_to_front<15 in hwy mode or <10 in urban mode)'. In PlantUML semantics, the text after the colon is one trigger field. The closed model correctly declares this as a single opaque event. The NL requires each condition to independently enable the transition (using 'or' to list alternatives). In UML, independently triggerable conditions require either separate transitions with distinct triggers/guards, or a single transition with a disjunctive guard. A single opaque event string cannot be decomposed at runtime, so none of the individual conditions can trigger the transition on its own. The strongest rebuttal ('the closed model is consistent with itself') addresses provenance but not the NL violation - the model fails to provide the NL-required independent condition enforcement.

In PlantUML semantics, the text after the colon is one trigger field. The closed model correctly declares this as a single opaque event. The NL requires each condition to independently enable the transition (using 'or' to list alternatives). In UML, independently triggerable conditions require either separate transitions with distinct triggers/guards, or a single transition with a disjunctive guard. contract.normative_statement: Each condition that may trigger collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active must be a separately triggerable event or guard.
contract.quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
